newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh in health scare.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh in health scare.

text.p: Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh, one of the communist country's ruling triumvirate, was reported to be unconscious in a Hanoi hospital on Sunday as doctors treated him for complications arising from blood-pressure problems.
Government officials who declined to be named said the 75-year-old general had been admitted to Hanoi's 108 Army hospital on Friday.
But widely varying reports of his condition made it difficult to accurately assess the seriousness of his illness.
A medical worker involved with the case said Anh had fallen ill over the past week, but his health had since improved and he might be discharged soon.
But separate government officials and political sources, who declined to be identified, said Anh was unconscious. They indicated his condition had become critical.
"It's really serious," one said. "They've started to make the preparations (for his death)."
One official said doctors had been struggling to cope with an unusually wide gap between Anh's upper and lower blood pressure readings.
He added that the president was also suffering haemorrhaging around the brain.

A veil of official secrecy was thrown around the hospital, which was barred to journalists. Official media made no mention of the president's condition, and presidential aides and advisers could not be contacted by phone.

State television, apparently reading from a foreign ministry news schedule issued several days ago, said Anh and his wife would be meeting with South Korea's President Kim Young-sam, who was due to visit later this week.
Hanoi's political rumour mill has been awash with speculation about the president's health over the past week because of several absences from public view.
His last reported activity by state media was the signing on Tuesday of a decision ratifying recent cabinet changes.

Anh is a key figure in Vietnam's leadership triumvirate, a collective system comprising three powerful figures chosen to ensure balance between different shades of socialist opinion and differing regional views.
The other members of the ruling trio are Communist Party chief Do Muoi, 79, seen as occupying a central and stabilising role in government, and the reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, 73.
Anh is widely viewed by Western observers as the most conservative of the three, and played a role in the normalising of Vietnamese-Chinese relations in 1991.

As president he is also seen as an essential part of the mechanism by which close party-army ties are ensured. Diplomats say the impact of his possible departure from Vietnam's political scene would depend largely on the choice of successor.
